attempts.summary: Implemented Ansible-managed, LVM-snapshot-backed recoverability for /srv/data on node1, orchestrated from node2 (the ansible-equipped control node). setup.yml provisions a loop-device-backed LVM volume group/logical volume mounted at /srv/data with boot-persistent systemd units; snapshot.yml takes an LVM snapshot; restore.yml unmounts, merges the snapshot back into the origin, and remounts, restoring exact prior content. Demonstrated end-to-end: seeded data, snapshotted, modified (deleted/corrupted/added files), restored, and verified checksums matched the pre-modification baseline exactly. During the mandatory reboot validation I found and fixed two real bugs in the boot-persistence systemd units (an ordering cycle, and a race causing the loop device to latch read-only before root remounted rw). Both node1 and node2 were then successfully restarted one at a time, each with proven boot-id changes and full unattended recovery of the data volume and Ansible control path.
